rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 4 (base_speed 1.1, kp 2.5, kd 0.3, narrow five-sensor array at x = 0.03, 0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03) is the best raced design at 302.3, with 11 of 20 oval finishes. Iteration 5 lowered base_speed to 0.9 and scored 136.2. Oval completion fell to 0 of 20, oval progress fell from 0.96 to 0.58, and oval line_loss_events rose from 0.95 to 1.85. So the speed drop hurt, and the Evaluator's pre-race reasoning that lower speed would cut line loss did not hold. The Evaluator's stated fallback for this case is to return to base_speed 1.1 and test kp 2.0 with kd 0.3 as a separate single-variable change. Iteration 2 (wide array) and iteration 3 (kp 2.2 with kd 0.25 at base_speed 1.3) both scored lower, so the geometry is kept and the kp/kd change is isolated here.

Change. Return base_speed to 1.1 and lower kp from 2.5 to 2.0. Everything else stays at the iteration 4 design: narrow geometry, sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], kd 0.3, ki 0, last_direction.

Expected result. Oval steering_oscillation (0.33 at kp 2.5) should fall because the proportional correction is smaller. Control_effort should fall too. Oval completion should hold near or above 50%, since the speed that worked is unchanged. The risk is the opposite: a weaker kp may leave the robot slower to correct on the tightest bends, which would show as higher max_error and line loss.

Hypotheses to test. (a) Part of the line loss comes from over-correction at kp 2.5, so kp 2.0 cuts line_loss_events and max_error on the s-bend and slalom. (b) Oval completion holds at or above the iteration 4 rate of 55%. Next step: if line loss falls and completion holds, test kd 0.25 alone. If line loss rises, return to kp 2.5 and test base_speed 1.2 alone, since 1.1 is the only tested speed between 0.9 (worse) and 1.3 (worse).
